11:1: You are to love Adonoy, your God, and you are to guard His watch [word], and His statutes, and His laws, and His commandments, all the years.
Therefore shall you love the Lord your God, and diligently observe His Word, His statutes, and His judgments always.
11:2: You will know today that not with your children who have not known and who have not seen the teaching of Adonoy, your God—His greatness, His powerful hand and His extended arm,
And know you this day, for (I speak) not with your children who have not known or seen the instruction of the law of the Lord your God, nor His greatness, nor His mighty hand, nor His uplifted arm,
11:3: and His signs and His deeds that He performed within Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, and to his entire land;
or His signs and works which He wrought in Mizraim, on Pharoh king of Mizraim, and on all the inhabitants of his land;
11:4: And what He did to the Egyptian army [host], to its horses and to its chariots—that He flooded the waters of Yam Suf over them when they were chasing you—Adonoy destroyed them until this day;

what He did also to the hosts of Mizraim, to their horses and chariots, when He made the waters of the Red Sea to overwhelm their faces when they followed after you, when the Lord destroyed them unto this day’s time;
11:5: And what He did for you in the wilderness, until you arrived at this place;
and what He hath done to you in the wilderness till the time that you came to this place;
11:6: And what He did to Dosson and to Avirom sons of Eli’ov son of Re’uven, that the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and [the members of] their families and their tents and all the sustenance at their feet [that was with them] amid all of Yisroel.

and what He did unto Dathan and Abiram the sons of Eliab bar Reuben, when the earth opened her mouth and swallowed them up with the men of their house, and all their substance, in the midst of all Israel:
11:7: Rather your eyes have been witnessing the entire overwhelming activity of Adonoy that He has performed.
for with your eyes have you seen all the great work of the Lord which He hath wrought.
11:8: You will guard the entire mitzvah that I am commanding you today, in order that you be encouraged and will arrive in, [amd go up to,] and inherit the land that you are crossing over there to inherit.
Therefore shall you keep all the precepts which I command you this day, that you may be strengthened, and go in, and inherit the land to possess which you go over;
11:9: And in order that you will last long on the land that Adonoy swore to your forefathers to give to them and to their descendants, a land flowing [producing] milk and honey.
and that your days may be multiplied upon the land which the Lord sware to your fathers to give it to them and their children; a land whose fruits are rich as milk, and sweet as honey.
11:10: For the land where you are arriving to inherit is not like the land of Egypt from which you departed, where you planted your seed and watered [it] on foot like a vegetable garden.
For the land to which thou goest in to possess it is not like the land of Mizraim, from whence you have come, in which thou didst sow thy seed, and water it thyself as a garden of herbs;
11:11: Rather, the land where you are crossing to inherit is a land of mountains and plains—by the rain of the skies will you drink water.
but the land which you pass over to inherit is a land of mountains and valleys: it drinketh water from the rain that cometh down from the heavens;
11:12: A land that Adonoy, your God, looks after; the eyes of Adonoy, your God, are always upon it, from the year’s beginning until the year’s end.
it is a land which the Lord your God inquireth after by His Word, that He may bless it evermore; the eyes of the Lord your God look upon it from the beginning of the year to the year’s end.
11:13: Should you thoroughly heed My commandments that I am commanding you today—to love Adonoy, your God, and to serve [before] Him with all your desires and with your entire beings,
And it shall be that if you diligently obey My commandments which I command you this day, to love the Lord your God, and to serve Him with all your heart, and with all your soul,
11:14: I will provide the rain of your land in its time, fall rain and spring rain, and you will harvest your grain and your wine and your olive oil.
then will I give you the rain of your land in its time, the early in Marchesvan, and the latter in Nisan, that you may gather in your corn, your wine., and your oil.
11:15: And I will provide grass in your field for your animals, and you will eat and be full.
I will give herbage also in thy field for thy cattle, that thou mayest eat and have enough.
11:16: Look out for yourselves lest your heart be misled [mistaken] and you turn away and serve other gods [idols of the nations] and bow to them,
Take heed to yourselves, lest you be led away by the imagination of your heart, and turn aside to serve the idols of the Gentiles, and worship them,
11:17: And Adonoy’s anger will be aroused against you, and He will restrain the skies and there will be no rain, and the soil will not yield its produce, and you will swiftly be removed from upon the good land that Adonoy is giving you.

and the Lord’s anger be provoked against you, and He shut up the clouds of heaven, and let not the rain come down, and the earth yield no provender, and you perish soon from off the glorious land which the Lord shall give you.
11:18: You are to place these words of Mine on your mind and on your being, and bind them as a sign on your hand and they will be totafos [tefillin] on your head;

But lay these my words upon your heart, and upon your soul, and bind them, written upon tephillin, as a sign upon the upper part (wrist?) of your left hands, and let them be for tephillin over thy forehead between thy eyes.
11:19: And you are to teach them to your sons to speak in them when you sit at home, and when you journey on the road, and when you go to sleep, and when you rise;

And thou shalt teach them to thy children to study them when you are sitting in your house with your kindred, and when you are walking in the way, and in the evening when you lie down, and in the morning when you arise.
11:20: And you are to write them on the doorposts [and affix them to the lintels] of your home and your gateways.
And you shall write them upon parchment, upon the posts, and affix them to three (things), against thy chest, against the pillars of thy house, and against thy gates:
11:21: In order that they will be many—your years and the years of your children on the soil that Adonoy swore to your forefathers to give them, like the years of heaven on earth.
that your days and the days of your children may be multiplied on the land which the Lord sware to your fathers to give you, as the number of the days that the heavens abide over the earth.
11:22: For if you truly guard this entire mitzvah that I am commanding you to perform, to love Adonoy, your God, to walk in all His ways [that are correct before Him] and to cling to Him [come near to the fear of Him].
For if you diligently keep every commandment that I command you to do it, to love the Lord your God, and walk in all the ways that are right before Him, and cleave unto His fear,
11:23: Adonoy will expel all these nations before you, and you will inherit nations greater and more powerful than you.
then will the Word of the Lord drive out all these nations from before you, and you shall possess the heritage of nations greater and stronger than yourselves.
11:24: Every place that the sole of your foot steps on will be yours, from the wilderness and the Lebanon, form the river—the Euphrates River—up to the ultimate [western] sea, will be your boundary.

Every place where the sole of your foot shall tread will be yours, from the wilderness and the mountain; (among) your mountains shall be the house of the sanctuary, and from the great river, the River Phrat, unto the ocean sea, whose waters are (old as) the creation, on the western side shall be your limit.
11:25: No man will stand up to you; fear of you and awe of you will Adonoy, your God, place upon the surface of the entire land that you are stepping into, as He promised you.
Not a man will be able to stand before you; but the Lord your God will set the fear and dread of you upon the faces of all the inhabiters of the land that you tread upon, as it hath been told you.
11:26: Look, I place before you today, a blessing and a curse.
MOSHEH the prophet said: Behold, I have this day set in order before you a Blessing and its contrary:
11:27: The blessing—that you heed [obey] the commandments of Adonoy, your God, that I am commanding you today.
the Blessing, if you will be obedient to the commandments of the Lord your God which I command you this day;
11:28: And the curse—if you do not heed the commandments of Adonoy, your God, and you veer from the course which I command you this day, to follow other gods [idols of the nations] which you did not know.

and its contrary, if you will not obey the commandments of the Lord your God, but will go astray from the path which I have taught you this day, in turning aside after the idols of the nations whom thou hast not known.
11:29: When Adonoy, your God, has brought you to the land that you are coming to inherit, you shall place the blessers on Mount Gerizim and the cursers on Mount Eival.

And it shall be, when the Lord your God will have brought you to the land into which you are going, to possess it, you shall place six tribes upon the mountain of Gerizim, and six tribes on the mountain of Ebal. They who recite the blessings shall turn their faces towards Mount Gerizim, and they who recite the curses shall turn their faces towards Mount Ebal.
11:30: Are they not across the Yardein and far beyond, along the route of the sunset? In the land of the Canaanites who dwell on the Arava Plain, opposite Gilgol, next to the [at the side of] Moreh Plain.
Are they not situated beyond Jordan by the way of the sunset, in the land of the Kenaanah, who dwell in the plain over against Gilgela by the side (of the place) of the vision of Mamre?
11:31: For you shall pass across the Yardein to come to inherit the land that Adonoy, your God, is giving you; you will inherit it and will dwell in it.
For you are to pass over Jordan to enter and possess the land which the Lord your God giveth you, and you will hold and will dwell therein.
11:32: You will guard to fulfill all the statutes and the laws that I am setting before you today.
Look well, therefore, that you perform all the statutes and judgments that I have set before you this day.
12:1: These are the statutes and the laws that you will guard to fulfill in the land that Adonoy, God of your forefathers, has given to inherit, all the years that you are alive on the land.
These are the statutes and judgments which you are to observe to do in the land which the Lord God of your fathers giveth you to inherit all the days that you live upon the earth.
12:2: You must obliterate all the places where the nations worshipped, whom you are inheriting, their gods [idols], on the high mountains, and on the hills, and under every evergreen tree.
You shall utterly destroy all the places in which the people (whose land) you will possess have worshipped their idols, upon the high mountains and hills, and under every tree of beautiful form.
12:3: You are to break apart their altars, and you are to smash their pillars, and their asherahs are you to burn in fire, and the statues of their gods [idols] are you to cut down; and you are to obliterate their name from that place.
You shall lay their altars in ruin, break down their pillars, burn their abominations with fire, and utterly destroy the images of their gods, and abolish their names from that place.
12:4: Do not act this way to [before] Adonoy, your God.
Not so may you do to blot out the inscription of the Name of the Lord your God.
12:5: Rather at the place that Adonoy, your God, chooses from all your tribes to set His Presence [have His Shechinah dwell] there, [at the abode of His Shechinah] will you seek His Presence and come there.
But in the land which the Word of the Lord your God will choose out of all your tribes for His Shekinah to dwell there, unto the place of His Shekinah shall you have recourse, and come thither,
12:6: You are to bring there your burnt-offerings and your sacred-offerings, and your tithes and the elevation of your hands [hand-offerings], and your pledges, and your donations, and the firstborn of your cattle and your flocks.
and bring your sacrifices and consecrated oblations, your tythes, the separation of your hands, your vows, your voluntary offerings, and the firstlings of your herds and flocks.
12:7: You are to eat there before Adonoy, your God, and you will be happy with the sum of your handiwork, you and [the members of] your households, as Adonoy, your God, has blessed you.
And you shall there eat before the Lord your God, and rejoice in all that you put your hand unto, you and your households, in which the Lord your God will have blessed you.
12:8: You may not do everything we do here today, each what is upright in his eyes [before him].
It will not be lawful for you to do (there) as we do here today, whatever any one thinks fit for himself;
12:9: For you will not have come as yet to the peace [the place of tranquility] and to the territory that Adonoy, your God, is giving you.
for you are not yet come to the Sanctuary, to the dwelling of Peace, and to the inheritance of the land which the Lord your God will give you.
12:10: When you cross the Yardein and settle in the land that Adonoy, your God, is apportioning to you, and He has granted you peace from all your enemies around, and you will live secure.

But when you have passed over Jordan and dwell in the land which the Lord your God will give you to inherit, and He hath given you repose from all your enemies round about, then shall you build the house of the Sanctuary, and afterward shall dwell securely.
12:11: Let it be that the place where Adonoy, your God, chooses to place His Presence [Shechinah] therein—it is there you shall bring all that I am commanding you: your burnt-offerings and your sacred-offerings, your tithes and your hand-offerings, and your choice promissory offerings that you pledge to [before] Adonoy.

And to the place which the Word of the Lord will choose to make His Shekinah to dwell there, shall you bring all your oblations, firstlings, and tythes, which I command you; there shall you offer your sacrifices and hallowed victims, there eat your tythes and the separation of your hands, and all your goodly vows which you may have vowed before the Lord.
12:12: You are to rejoice in the presence of Adonoy, your God, you and your sons and your daughters, your male slaves and your female slaves, and the Levite who is in your cities, for he has no portion or territory with you.
And you shall rejoice before the Lord your God, you and your sons and daughters, your servants and handmaids, and the Levite who is in your cities, for he hath no portion or inheritance with you.
12:13: Take heed, lest you offer up your burnt-offerings anywhere you envision as proper.
Beware lest you offer your sacrifices in any place which thou mayest see;
12:14: Solely in the place that Adonoy chooses within one of your tribes, there are you to offer up your burnt-offerings, and there are you to do everything that I am commanding you.
but in the Place which the Lord will choose in the inheritance of one of your tribes, there shall you offer your sacrifices and do whatever I command you.
12:15: Except with the fullness of your appetite you may slaughter and eat meat in accord with the blessing of Adonoy, your God, that He has given you in all your cities; the ritually unclean and the clean will eat it like the [meat of the] deer and the gazelle.

Nevertheless, after every wish of your soul, you may kill and eat flesh according to the blessing of the Lord your God, which He will give you in all your cities; they who are unclean so as not to be able to offer holy things, and they who are clean that they may offer holy things, may eat of it alike, as the flesh of the antelope or of the hart.
12:16: However, you may not eat the blood; on the earth are you to spill it like water.
Only be careful to pour out the blood upon the ground like water.
12:17: You are not permitted to eat in your cities the tithe of your grain and your wine and your olive oil, and the first-born of your cattle and your flocks, and all your pledges that you pledge, and your donations and the terumah-separation of your hand-offerings].

It will not be lawful for you to eat the tenths of your corn, or wine, or oil, or the firstlings of your herd or flock, nor any of the vows that you have vowed, or freewill offerings, or the separation of your hands in your cities;
12:18: Rather, before Adonoy, your God, are you to eat it, in the place that Adonoy, your God, chooses—you and your son and your daughter, and your male slave and your female slave, and the Levite in your cities; and you will be happy in the presence of Adonoy, your God, with the sum of your handiwork.

but you shall eat it before the Lord your God, in the place which the Lord your God will choose; you, and your sons and daughters, and your handmaids, and the Levites who are in your cities; and you shall rejoice before the Lord your God, in all that thou puttest thine hand unto.
12:19: Watch yourself, lest you forsake the Levite, all your years on your land.
Beware that thou aggrieve not the Levite all your days in which you dwell in your land.
12:20: When Adonoy, your God, expands your border as He promised you, and you say, ‘‘I would like to eat meat’’ because you have an appetite to eat meat; to the full extent of your appetite eat meat.

When the Lord your God will have enlarged your border, as He hath said unto you; and thou sayest, I would eat flesh, because thy soul may desire to eat flesh, thou mayest eat flesh according to all thy desire.
12:21: When the place is distant from you that Adonoy, your God, chooses to set His Presence [Shechinah] there, you may slaughter some of your cattle or your flocks that Adonoy gave you, as I have commanded you; and you will eat in your cities with all your appetite.

But if the place which the Lord your God will have chosen that His Shekinah may dwell there be too far off, then may you eat of your herds and flocks which the Lord your God shall give you, as I have com- manded you, in your cities you may eat, according to all the desire of your soul:
12:22: Only, as the [meat of the] dear and the gazelle may be eaten, so may you eat it; the ritually unclean and the clean together may eat it.
as the flesh of the antelope or hart so may you eat it; he who is unclean that he may not offer holy things, and he who is clean that he may offer them, may eat of it alike.
12:23: Only, exercise strength in not eating [in order not to eat] the blood, for the blood is the life; and do not eat the spirit with the meat.
Only put a strong restraint upon your desires, that you eat no blood; for the blood is the subsistence of the life. You may not, with the flesh, eat blood, in which is the subsistence of life:
12:24: Do not eat it; onto the earth are you to spill it like water.
you shall not eat it, you shall pour it out upon the ground like water:
12:25: Do not eat it, so that you may enjoy beneficience, and your children after you, when you do the upright [proper] in Adonoy’s eyes.
eat it not, that it may be well with you, and with your children after you, while you do that which is right before the Lord.
12:26: However, your sacred offerings [tithes] that you will have, and your pledges, you are to bring when you come to the place that Adonoy chooses.
Nevertheless, animals which are your consecrated tenths, and your votive offerings, you shall take and bring to the place which the Lord will choose;
12:27: You are to execute your burnt-offerings—the meat and the blood—on the altar of Adonoy, your God; and the blood of your peace [sacred]-offerings will be poured on the altar of Adonoy, your God, then you will eat the meat.

and thou shalt do (with them) according to the rite of thy burnt offerings, (and offer) the flesh and the blood upon the altar of the Lord thy God: the blood of the rest of thy holy oblations shall be poured out at the altar of the Lord thy God, but of the flesh it is lawful to eat.
12:28: Preserve and heed [obey] all these words that I am commanding you, in order that you have it good and your children after you forever, when you do that which is good and that which is upright [correct and proper before] in the eyes of Adonoy, your God.
Observe and obey all these words that I command you, that it may be well with you and with your children after you for ever, while you do that which is good and right before the Lord your God.
12:29: When Adonoy, your God, will have eliminated the nations whom you are coming there to inherit, from before you; and you inherit them and dwell in their land;
When the Lord your God shall have cut off the nations among whom you go, and have expelled them from before you, and you inherit and dwell in their land,
12:30: Look out for yourself, lest you are torn apart along with them, after they have been annihilated before you, and lest you inquire about their gods [idols], saying, ‘‘How did these nations worship their gods, let me do so, too.’’

beware that you stumble not after their idols when they shall have been destroyed before you, or lest you seek after their idols, saying, How did these peoples worship their gods, that we may worship as they did?
12:31: Do not do so to [before] Adonoy, your God, because whatever is abominated by [distanced before] God, what He hates, they have done for their gods [idols]; for even their sons and their daughters do they burn in fire to their gods [idols].

So shall you not do in serving the Lord your God; for whatever is abominable and hateful to Him have they done to their idols; for even their sons and daughters they have bound and burned with fire unto their idols.
12:32: Everything that I am commanding you—be careful to fulfill it; do not add to it and do not subtract from it.
Whatsoever I command you, that shall you observe to do; ye shall not add to it nor diminish from it.
13:1: If a prophet arises among you or a dreamer of a dream, and he gives you an omen or a miracle,
When there may arise among you a false prophet or a dreamer of a profane dream, and he give you a sign or a miracle,
13:2: And the omen or the miracle happens—the one he told you about—saying, ‘‘Let us go after other gods [idols of other nations], that you do not know, and let us serve them.’’
and the sign or the miracle come to pass, (yet) because he spake with you, saying, Let us go after the gods of the peoples whom thou hast not known, and worship them,
13:3: Do not listen to [accept] the words of that prophet or to that dreamer of a dream, because Adonoy, your God, is testing you to know whether you love Adonoy, your God, wholeheartedly and with your entire beings.

you shall not hearken to the words of that lying prophet, or him who hath dreamed that dream; for the Lord your God (thereby) trieth you, to know whether you will love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul.
13:4: After [the fear of] Adonoy, your God, are you to go, fear Him, keep His commandments, heed His voice [accept His word], serve [before] Him, and cleave to [the fear of] Him.
You shall walk after the service of the Lord your God, and Him shall you fear, and keep His commandments, hearken to His word, pray before Him, and cleave unto His fear.
13:5: And that prophet or that dreamer of a dream is to be executed, for he has uttered a fabrication about Adonoy, your God—Who took you out of the land of Egypt, and Who redeemed you from the house of bondage—to mislead you from the way that Adonoy, your God, commanded you to go upon, and you will eliminate the evil [doers] from within you.

And that prophet of lies, or that dreamer of dreams, shall be slain with the sword, because he had spoken perversity against the Lord your God who brought you out from the land of the Mizraee, and redeemed you from the house of the affliction of slaves to make you to go astray from the path which the Lord your God hath commanded you to walk in: so shall you bring down the doers of evil among you.
13:6: If one shall incite you, your brother—son of your mother—or your son or your daughter, or the wife of your bosom [covenant], or your neighbor who is your soul mate, clandestinely, saying, ‘‘Let us go and serve other gods [idols of other nations]’’ whom you never knew—neither you nor your forefathers.

When thy brother, the son of thy mother, when even the son of thy father, or thy own son or thy daughter, or thy wife who reposeth with thee, or thy friend who is beloved as thy soul, shall give thee evil counsel, to make thee go astray, speaking out and saying, Let us go and worship the gods of the Gentiles, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known;
13:7: From the gods [idols] of the nations that surround you, who are near you or at a distance from you, from the ends of the earth to the ends of the earth,
or the idols of the seven nations who are near you round about, or of the rest of the nations who are far away from you, from one end of the earth to the other;
13:8: Do not be favorbly inclined towards him, and do not listen to [accept from] him; and do not view him compassionately, and do not take pity and do not cover for him.
you shall not consent to them, nor hearken to him, neither shall your eye spare him or have compassion, nor shall you hide him in secret;
13:9: For you must surely execute him. Let your hand strike him first to execute him, and the hand of the entire people afterward.
but killing you shall kill him; your hand shall be the first upon him to slay him, and afterwards the hand of all the people;
13:10: And you are to stone him with stones so that he dies, for he sought to mislead you from [the fear of] Adonoy, your God, Who took you out of the land of Egypt, from the house of slavery.

and you shall stone him that he die; because he sought to draw them away from the fear of the Lord thy God, who brought you out free from the land of Mizraim, from the house of the affliction of slaves.
13:11: And all of Yisroel will hear and will fear, and they will not proceed to do so evil a thing as this, within you.
And all Israel will hear and be afraid, and never more do according to that evil thing among you.
13:12: If you hear in one of your cities that Adonoy, your God, is giving you in which to settle, the following:
When, in one of your cities which the Lord your God will give you to dwell in, you hear it said
13:13: ‘‘Men have gone out—unscrupulous [evil]—from among you, and they have misled the inhabitants of their city by saying, ‘Let us go and serve other gods [idols of other nations]’ that you do not know.’’

that (certain) men of pride are drawing back from the doctrine of the Lord your God, or that even sages of your rabbins have gone forth and led away the inhabitants of their city, saying, Let us go and worship the gods of the nations which you have not known:
13:14: You must investigate, inquire, and interrogate thoroughly; and if in fact the report is true and accurate—this abomination was committed among you.
then search you out, and examine with witnesses, and make good inquiry; and, behold, if the thing be true and certain that this abomination hath been really done among you,
13:15: You must surely strike down the inhabitants of that city by the sword; annihilate it and everything that is in it, and its livestock by the sword.
you shall smite the inhabitants of that city with the edge of the sword, to destroy it utterly and whatever is therein, even its cattle, with the edge of the sword.
13:16: And all its booty are you to collect within its plaza, and you are to burn in fire the city and all its booty—totally—for [before] Adonoy, your God; and it will be a ruin forever, it is never to be rebuilt.

You shall gather all its spoil into the midst of the street, and burn the city with fire, together with the whole of the spoil, before the Lord your God; and it shall be a desolate heap for ever, never to be builded again:
13:17: Let nothing of the cherem cling to your hand; so that Adonoy withdraws His raising fury and grant you mercy, and He will be merciful toward you and multiply you as He swore to your forefathers
that the Lord may be turned from the fierceness of His anger, and may show His mercy upon you, and love you, and multiply you, as He hath sworn to your fathers.
13:18: When you heed the voice [accept the word] of Adonoy, your God, to guard all His commandments that I am commanding you today, to do the upright [proper before] in the eyes of Adonoy, your God.
So be ye obedient to the Word of the Lord your God, to keep all His commandments which I command you this day, that you may do what is right before the Lord your God.
14:1: You are sons to [before] Adonoy, your God; do not lacerate yourselves and do not make yourselves bald between your eyes for a dead person.
As beloved children before the Lord your God, you shall not make lacerations in your flesh, nor make bare the crown of the hair over your foreheads on account of the soul of the dead.
14:2: For you are a sacred people to Adonoy, your God, and Adonoy has chosen you to be for Him a treasured people from all the peoples who are on the surface of the earth.
For you are to be a holy people before the Lord your God: the Lord your God hath chosen you to be a people more beloved than all the peoples who are upon the face of the earth.
14:3: You may not eat of any thing that for you is abominable.
14:4: These are the animals that you are to eat: the bovine, the sheep and the goat;
These are the animals which you may eat: oxen, and lambs of the ewes, such as are not blemished (unclean), and kids of the goats unmixed with what are unclean.
14:5: The gazelle, the deer and the fallow deer; and the ibex and the adax; and the wild ox and the wild sheep.
Harts and antelopes and fallow deer, rock goats and reems, wild oxen and pygargs;
14:6: And every animal whose sole is cloven, whose hoof is truly split in two, regurgitating [its] cud within the animals, it may you eat.
and every animal that hath the divided hoof, and horns, and that cleaveth the cleft, bringing up the cud among animals, that you may eat.
14:7: These, however, do not eat from the regurgitators of cud and from the cloven-soled [split into hooves]: the dromedary, the camel, and the hare and the hyrax; for regurgitators of cud are they, but have no cloven sole; they are ritually unclean for you.

But of these you may not eat that bring up the cud, or of those who (only) have the hoof divided, the cast thing (embryo) which hath two heads or a double back, things which are not to be perpetuated in the same species (i.e. as a species); nor the camel, the hare, or the coney, because they chew the cud, but do not divide the hoof; they are unclean to you.
14:8: Also the pig, because it is cloven-soled but does not [regurgitate its] cud; it is ritually unclean for you. From their flesh do not eat, and do not come in contact [near] with their carcasses.

The swine, because, though he hath the hoof divided, and there is none produced that like him divideth (the hoof), and yet cheweth not the cud, is unclean to you; of their flesh you shall not eat, nor touch their dead bodies.
14:9: These are you to eat from whatever is in the water: whatever has fins and scales may you eat.

But this you may eat, of all that are in the waters, whatever hath fins to move, as by flying, and scales upon its skin; and though (some of which) may fall away, yet if there remain on under its jaw, another under its fin, and another under its tail, that you may eat.
14:10: And whatever does not have fins and scales do not eat; they are ritually unclean for you.
But whatever hath neither fins nor scales you may not eat; it is unclean to you.
14:11: You may eat any pure bird.
Every bird which hath a vesicle or crop which may be picked away, and which (bird) is longer than a finger, and not of the rapacious kind, you may eat.
14:12: And this is what you may not eat: the griffon vulture and the bearded vulture, and the black vulture;
But these are they which you may not eat: the eagle, the ossifrage, the osprey,
14:13: The ra’ah and the ayah, and the kite according to its kind;
the daitha (lammer geyer?) white or black, which is a bird of prey, a kind of vulture.
14:14: And every raven according to its kind;
And every raven after his kind;
14:15: And the dark desert eagle owl and the kestrel, and the gull, and the sparrow hawk according to its kind;
and the owl, and nighthawk, and the cuckoo, and the falcon after his kind;
14:16: The dark little owl and the long-eared owl, and the tinshames;
the great owl, and the sea gull (catcher of fish from the sea), and the night owl,
14:17: And the light little owl and the Egyptian vulture, and the shalach;
and the cormorant white or black, and the pica,
14:18: And the stork, and the heron according to its kind, and the duchifas, and the bat.
and the stork white or black after its kind, and the heathcock, and the bat,
14:19: And all flying creeping creatures are ritually unclean for you; they may not be eaten.
and all flies (bees) and wasps, and all worms of vegetables and pulse, which come away from (materials of) food and fly as birds, are unclean to you, they may not be eaten;
14:20: Every ritually clean bird you may eat.
but any clean beast {locust} you may eat.
14:21: Do not eat any carcass; to the [uncircumcised] alien in your cities give it and he will eat it or sell it to a non-Jew [foreigner], for you are a people sanctified to Adonoy, your God; do not cook a kid in its mother’s milk [milk with meat].

You shall not eat of anything that is unclean through the manner of its death; you may give it to the uncircumcised stranger who is in your cities to eat it, or sell it to a son of the Gentiles; for you are a holy people before the Lord your God. It shall not be lawful for you to boil, much less to eat, flesh with milk when both are mixed together.
14:22: You must surely tithe all the produce of your planting, that your field yields on a yearly basis.
Be mindful to tythe your fruitage of whatsoever cometh forth, and which you gather in from the field year by year; not giving the fruit of one year for the fruit of another.
14:23: You shall eat in the presence of Adonoy, your God, in the place He chooses to house His Presence [Shechinah] there—the tithe of your grain, your wine, and your olive oil, and the firstborn of your cattle and flocks; in order that you learn to fear [before] Adonoy, your God, all the years.

And the second tythe you shall eat before the Lord your God in the place which He will choose to make His Shekinah to dwell there; the tenths of your corn, your vines, and your oil, and likewise the firstlings of your oxen and sheep, that you may learn to fear the Lord your God all the days.
14:24: If the journey will be beyond you; if you will be unable to carry it because the place is distant for you where Adonoy, your God, chooses to set His Presence [Shechinah] there, for Adonoy, your God, has blessed you—

And if the way be too great for you to be able to carry the tenth, because the place which the Lord thy God will choose for His Shekinah to dwell there is too distant from you, when the Lord thy God shall have blessed thee,
14:25: you will substitute coins. You will bundle the coins in your hand, and will go to the place that Adonoy, your God, chooses.
then thou mayest make exchange for it into silver, and bind the sum in thy hand, and proceed to the place which the Lord thy God shall choose,
14:26: You will spend the money for anything you desire—for cattle, sheep, wine, intoxicating liquor [fresh and aged wine]—and for anything that you wish; and you will eat there in the presence of Adonoy, your God, and will rejoice, you and [the members of] your household.

and give the silver for any thing that thy soul pleaseth, of oxen, sheep, wine new or old, or whatever thy soul desireth; and you shall eat there before the Lord your God and rejoice, you and the men of your house.
14:27: And the Levite who is in your city, you must not abandon; since he has no portion or inheritance with you.
And the Levite who is in your cities forsake not, for he hath not a portion or a heritage with you.
14:28: At the end of three years, separate all the tithes of your produce of that year and set them aside in your city.
At the end of three years you shall bring forth all the tenths of your produce for that year, and lay them up in your cities.
14:29: The Levite shall come, for he has no portion or inheritance with you, and the proselyte and the orphan and the widow who are in your city, let them eat their fill; in order that Adonoy, your God, bless you in all the endeavors that you make.

And the Levite, because he hath no part or heritage with you, and the stranger, the orphan, and the widow who are in your cities, shall come and eat and be satisfied; that the Lord your God may bless you in all the works of your hands that you do.
15:1: At the end of seven years, you are to make shemitah.
At the end of seven years you shall make a Release.
15:2: And this is the statement of shemitah: suspend every creditor’s hand from his loan to his neighbor; he will not claim [it] from his neighbor or his brother because it was proclaimed shemitah to [before] Adonoy.

And this is the indication of the custom of the Release: Every man who is master of a loan, who lendeth to his neighbour, shall give remission. He shall not have power to coerce his neighbour in demanding his loan, nor of his brother, a son of Israel; because the beth din hath published the Release before the Lord.
15:3: You should demand payment from the stranger [foreigner], but what you have with your brother your hand will relinquish.
From a son of the Gentiles thou mayest exact, but the lawful right (dina) which is thine with thy brother thou shalt release with thine hand.
15:4: End it [poverty], so that there will be no one, destitute among you when Adonoy will surely bless you in the land that Adonoy, your God, is giving you as territory to inherit.

If you will only be diligent in the precepts of the law, there will be no poor among you; for, blessing, the Lord will bless you in the land which the Lord your God will give you for a possession to inherit;
15:5: Only if you will listen to [heed] the voice [word] of Adonoy, your God, to guard to fulfill this entire mitzvah that I am commanding you today.
if, obeying, you will only obey the Word of the Lord your God, to observe and do all these commandments which I command you this day.
15:6: When Adonoy, your God, blesses you just as He told you, you will grant loans to nations but you will not borrow; and you will rule over many nations, but over you they will not rule.

For the Lord your God blesseth you, as He saith to you (that) you shall take from many nations, but they will not take from you; and you will have power over many nations, but they shall not have power over you.
15:7: If there should be someone destitute in your midst among one of your brothers in one of your cities, in your land that Adonoy, your God, is giving you; do not harden your heart and do not close your hand against your destitute brother.

But if you be not diligent in the precepts of the law, and there be among you a poor man in one of thy cities of the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, thou shalt not harden thy heart, nor hold back thy hand from thy poor brother;
15:8: Rather, you must surely open your hand generously to him, and you must surely extend a loan to him to cover the wants [the measure of that] which he lacks.
but thou shalt open thy hand to him, and lend to him according to the measure of his want through which he is in need.
15:9: Look out for yourself lest there be an evil thought in your mind, saying, ‘‘The seventh year is approaching, the shemitah year,’’ and you will look askance at your destitute brother and will not give him; and if he cries out concerning you to Adonoy, you will be regarded as sinful.

Beware lest there be a word in thy proud heart, saying: The seventh year, the year of release, is at hand, and your eye become evil toward your poor brother, so as to be not willing to give to him, and he cry against you to the Lord, and there be guilt upon you.
15:10: You must surely give him, and let your heart not hurt when you give him; for, as a consequence of this thing, Adonoy, your God, will bless you in all your work and in all your commerce.
Giving you shall give to him, nor shall your heart be evil when you give to him; for on account of this matter the Lord your God will bless you in all your works that you put your hands unto.
15:11: For the destitute will not cease to exist within the land; therefore I am commanding you saying, ‘‘Open your hand generously to your brother, to your indigent, and to your destitute in your land.’’

But forasmuch as the house of Israel will not rest in the commandments of the law, the poor will not cease in the land: therefore I command you, saying: You shall verily open your hands toward your neighbours, to the afflicted around you, and to the poor of your country.
15:12: If your brother—Jew or Jewess—is sold to you and he serves you six years; then in the seventh year you are to send him free from you.
If your brother, a son of Israel, or if a daughter of Israel, be sold to you, he shall serve you six years; and when the seventh comes, thou shalt send him from you free.
15:13: When you send him [a] free [man] from you, do not send him away empty-handed.
And when thou lettest him go away from thee at liberty, thou shalt not send him away empty.
15:14: You must surely present him with a severance bonus from your flocks, and from your threshing area, and your wine cellar, whatever Adonoy, your God, has blessed you with are you to give him.
Comforting thou shalt comfort him out of your flocks, your floors, and your wine presses; as the Lord hath blessed you ye shall give to him.
15:15: Remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt and Adonoy, your God, redeemed you; that is why I am commanding you this matter today.
And be mindful that you were servants in the land of Mizraim, and that the Lord your God set you free; therefore I command you today that you do this thing.
15:16: Should he say to you, ‘‘I am not leaving you;’’ because he loves you and [the members of] your household, for he has it good with you.
But if he say to thee, I will not go out from thee, because I love thee and the men of thy house, and because it hath been good for him to be with thee,
15:17: Take the awl and put it through his ear and the door, and he will become your perpetual slave [ministering servant]. And do the same to your maid-servant as well.

then thou shalt take an awl, and bore (or apply) it through his ear, and that to the door of the house of judgment, and he shall be thy serving servant until the Jubilee. And for thy handmaid also thou shalt write a certificate of release, and give it to her.
15:18: Let it not seem difficult to you when you send him [a] free [man] from you, for double [two for one] the profit produced by the wage earner has he worked for you six years; and Adonoy, your God, will bless you in everything you do.

It must not be a hardship in thy eyes when thou sendest him away from thee; for double the hire of an hireling hath he been of service to thee six years; and on his account the Lord thy God hath blessed thee in all that thou hast done.
15:19: Every firstborn that is born in your cattle, and in your flocks—a male—you must consecrate to Adonoy, your God; you may not work with your first-born ox, or shear the first-born of your flocks.
Every firstling male that cometh of thy herd and flock thou shalt consecrate before the Lord thy God. Thou shalt not work with the firstlings of your herd, nor shear the firstlings of your flocks;
15:20: Before Adonoy, your God, you must eat it, each year, in the place that Adonoy chooses, you and [the members of] your household.
you shall eat thereof before the Lord your God from year to year, in the place which the Lord will choose, you and the men of your houses.
15:21: And if it has a blemish—if it is crippled or blind—or has any severe blemish, do not slaughter it to Adonoy, your God.
But if there be any spot in it, if it be lame or blind, or have any blemish, you shall not sacrifice it before the Lord your God:
15:22: In your cities may you eat it; the ritually unclean and the clean together, like the [meat of the] deer and the gazelle.
you may eat it in your cities; he who is unclean, (so) that he may not approach to holy things, and he who being clean may approach the holy, may alike (eat), as the flesh of the antelope or hart.
15:23: Only, do not eat its blood; spill it like water on the ground.
Only you shall not eat the blood; you shall pour it out upon the ground like water.
16:1: Take heed of [observe] the month of spring, when you will celebrate Pesach for [before] Adonoy your God; for in the month of spring Adonoy, your God, took you out from Egypt [and performed miracles for you] at night.

Be mindful to keep the times of the festivals, with the intercalations of the year, and to observe the rotation thereof: in the month of Abiba to perform the pascha before the Lord your God, because in the month of Abiba the Lord your God brought you out of Mizraim; you shall eat it therefore by night.
16:2: You shall slaughter the pesach-offering to [before] Adonoy, your God, flocks of ruminants [young lambs] and cattle [sacred offerings of oxen] in the place that Adonoy chooses to house His Presence [Shechinah] there.

But you shall sacrifice the pascha before the Lord your God between the suns; and the sheep and the bullocks on the morrow, on that same day to rejoice in the feast at the place which the Lord will choose to make His Shekinah to dwell there.
16:3: Do not eat chometz on it; seven days are you to eat on it matzos, bread of anguish; since in haste you left the land of Egypt, so that you remember the day of your exodus from the land of Egypt all the days of your life.

You shall not eat leavened bread with the pascha; seven days you shall eat unleavened bread unto His Name, the unleavened bread of humiliation; for with haste you went forth from the land of Mizraim; that you may remember the day of your outgoing from the land of Mizraim all the days of your life.
16:4: And no sourdough of yours may be seen in all of your boundary seven days; and none of the flesh may remain overnight which you slaughtered towards the evening of the first day—until morning.

Take heed that in the beginning of the pascha there be no leaven seen among you within all your borders for seven days; and that none of the flesh which you sacrifice in the evening of the first day remain till the morning.
16:5: You are forbidden [have no permission] to slaughter the pesach in any of your cities that Adonoy, your God, is giving you.
It will not be allowed you to eat the pascha in (any) one of your cities which the Lord your God giveth to you;
16:6: Solely in the place that Adonoy, your God, chooses to house His Presence [Shechinah], there will you slaughter the pesach towards the afternoon, at sunset, at the time you left Egypt.

but in the place which the Lord your God will choose to make His Shekinah to dwell, there shall you sacrifice the pascha; and in the evening at the going down of the sun you may eat it until the middle of the night, the time when you began to go out of Mizraim.
16:7: You shall cook [it] and eat [it] in the place that Adonoy, your God, chooses; and you may depart in the morning and go to your residence.
And you shall dress and eat it in the place which the Lord your God will choose, and in the early morn (if need be) thou mayest return from the feast, and go to thy cities.
16:8: For six days you shall eat matzos, and on the seventh day, is one of withdrawal [assembly] for the sake of Adonoy, your God, do not do work.

On the first day thou shalt offer the omer, and eat unleavened cakes of the old corn; but in the six remaining days you may begin to eat unleavened cakes of the new corn, and on the seventh day you shall assemble with thanksgiving before the Lord your God; no work shall you perform.
16:9: Seven weeks count for yourself; from the time the sickle begins felling the standing grain, begin to count seven weeks.
Seven weeks number to you; from the time when you begin to put the sickle to the harvest of the field after the reaping of the omer you shall begin to number the seven weeks.
16:10: You are to celebrate the festival of Shovuos for [before] Adonoy, your God, to the fullness of your open-handed gift that you can give, as Adonoy, your God, has blessed you.
And you shall keep with joy the Festival of Weeks before the Lord your God, after the measure of the freewill offerings of your hands, according as the Lord your God shall have blessed you.
16:11: You are to rejoice in the presence of [before] Adonoy, your God—you, and your son and your daughter, and your male slave and your female slave, and the Levite who is in your city, and the proselyte, and the orphan and the widow who are among you—in the place that Adonoy, your God, chooses to house His Presence [Shechinah] there.

And you shall rejoice with the joy of the feast before the Lord your God, you and your sons, your daughters, your servants and handmaids, the Levites who are in your cities, and the stranger, the orphan, and the widow who are among you, at the place which the Lord your God will choose where to make His Shekinah to dwell.
16:12: Remember that you were a slave in Egypt; you are to guard and celebrate these statutes.
Remember that you were servants in Mizraim; so shall you observe and perform these statutes.
16:13: The festival of Sukkos celebrate for yourself seven days, when you harvest your threshing-floor and your wine-press.
The Feast of Tabernacles you shall make to you seven days, when you will have completed to gather in the corn from your threshing floors, and the wine from your presses.
16:14: You are to rejoice during your festival—you and your son and your daughter, and your male slave and your female slave, and the Levite and the proselyte, and the orphan and the widow who are in your city.

And you shall rejoice in the joy of your feasts with the clarinet and flute, you and your sons and daughters, your handmaids, the Levite, the stranger, the orphan, and the widow, who are in your cities.
16:15: Seven days are you to be festive for Adonoy, your God, in the place Adonoy chooses, for Adonoy, your God, will bless you in all your produce and in all your endeavors; and you shall experience pure joy.

Seven days you shall keep the feast before the Lord your God in the place which the Lord will choose, because the Lord your God will have blessed you in all your provision, and in all the work of your hands, and so shall you be joyful in prosperity.
16:16: Three times a year are all your males to be seen in the presence of [before] Adonoy, your God, in the place that He chooses—in the festival of Matzos, and on the festival of Shovuos, and on the festival of Sukkos—and he shall not appear in the presence of [before] Adonoy empty-handed.

Three times in the year shall all your males appear before the Lord your God in the place that He will choose; at the Feast of the Unleavened, at the Feast of Weeks, and at the Feast of Tabernacles; nor must you appear before the Lord your God empty of any of the requirements;
16:17: Everyone according to the gift appropriate to his means, according to the blessing of Adonoy, your God, that He gave you.
every one after the measure of the gifts of his hands, according to the blessing which the Lord your God hath bestowed upon you.
16:18: Judges and police officers you shall appoint for yourself in all of your cities that Adonoy, your God, is giving you for your tribes; who will judge the people righteous justice [true judgment].
UPRIGHT judges and efficient administrators you shall appoint in all your cities which the Lord your God will give you for your tribes, and they shall judge the people with true judgment.
16:19: Do not pervert justice; do not display favoritism; and do not accept bribery, for bribery blinds the eyes of the wise and distorts words that are just [perverts the words of justice].

You shall not set judgment aside, nor respect persons, nor take a gift, because a gift blindeth the eyes of the wise who take it; for it perverteth them to foolishness, and confuseth equitable words in the mouth of the judges in the hour of their decision
16:20: Pursue absolute justice so that you may live and inherit the land that Adonoy, your God, is giving you.
Upright and perfect judgment in truth shalt thou follow, that you may come to inherit the land which the Lord your God will give you.
16:21: Do not plant an Asherah for yourself [or] any tree near the altar of Adonoy, your God, that you will make for yourself.
As it is not allowed you to plant a grove by the side of the Lord’s altar, so is it not allowed you to associate in judgment a fool with a wise judge to teach that which you are to do.
16:22: And do not erect for yourself a monument that Adonoy, your God, detests.
As it is not for you to erect a statue, so are you not to appoint to be a governor a proud man, whom the Lord your God doth abhor.
17:1: Do not sacrifice to [before] Adonoy, your God, an ox or a lamb that has a blemish, any bad thing; for it is abominated [distanced] by [before] Adonoy, your God.
You shall not sacrifice before the. Lord your God a bullock or lamb which hath any blemish or evil in it, or which is torn or rent; for that is abominable before the Lord your God.
17:2: If there is found among you, in one of your cities that Adonoy, your God, is giving you, a man or a woman who does what is evil in the eyes of Adonoy, your God, by violating His covenant.
If there be found among you in one of your cities that the Lord your God will give you a man or woman who doth what is evil before the Lord your God in transgressing His covenant,
17:3: He goes and serves other gods [idols of the nations] and bows to them—whether to the sun or to the moon or to any of the host of heaven that I did not command.
and, following after evil desire, shall serve the idols of the Gentiles, and worship them, or the sun, or the moon, or all the host of the heavens, which I have not commanded;
17:4: When you are told and you understand, you are to inquire thoroughly. If in fact the report is authenticated and accurate—this abomination was committed within Yisroel.
and it be told you, and you hear and make inquiry by witnesses fairly; and, behold, if this word be true and certain, that such abomination is wrought among you,
17:5: You are to take out that man or that woman who did this evil thing to your city [the door of your court]—the man or the woman—and you are to stone them with stones so that they die.
then you shall bring forth that man or woman who hath done this evil thing, unto the gate of your house of judgment, the man or the woman, and you shall stone them that they die.
17:6: By the speech of two witnesses or three witnesses is the guilty one [the one sentenced to death] to be executed; he is not to be executed by the oral testimonoy of one witness.
Upon the word of two witnesses or of three he shall die who is guilty of death; they shall not be put to death on the word of one witness.
17:7: Let the hand of the witnesses be against him first to execute him, and the hand of the entire people afterward; and you will eliminate the evil [doer] from within you.
The hands of the witnesses shall be first upon him to kill him, and afterward the hands of all (any of) the people; and so shall you bring down the evil doer among you.
17:8: If a matter of law is too abstruse for you—between blood and blood, between decision and decision, or between leprosy [a plague of confinement] and leprosy [a plague of confinement], matters under [legal] dispute in your city; you shall rise and ascend to the place that Adonoy, your God, will have chosen.

If there be with you an extraordinary matter for judgment between unclean and clean blood, cases of life or of money, or between a plague of leprosy or of the scall, with words of controversy in your beth din, then you shall arise and go up to the place which the Lord your God will choose;
17:9: You are to come before the kohanim-the Levites and the judge officiating during those days; you will inquire and they will tell you the legal decision.
and you shall come to the priests of the tribe of Levi, and to the judge who will be in those days, and inquire of them, and they will show you the process of judgment.
17:10: You are to act according to the word that they tell you from that place that Adonoy will have chosen; and you are to be careful to fulfill exactly as they instruct you.
Then shall you do according to the word of the custom of the law that they will show you at the place the Lord will choose, and observe to do whatsoever they teach you.
17:11: In accord with the Torah that they instruct you and upon the law that they state to you, are you to act; do not deviate from the word they tell you, neither right or left.

According to the word of the law that they will teach you, and the manner of judgment they pronounce, you shall do. You shall not turn aside from the sentence they will show you, to the right or to the left.
17:12: But the man who acts deliberately to not heed the kohein who stands to serve there [before] Adonoy, your God, or the judge; that man is to be executed and you will eliminate the evil [doer] from Yisroel.

And the man who will act with presumption, and not obey the judge or the priest who standeth there to minister before the Lord your God, that man shall be put to death; so shalt you put down the doer of evil from Israel,
17:13: Let all the people hear and fear, and not sin deliberately again.
and all the people will hear, and be afraid, and not do wickedly again.
17:14: When you arrive in the land that Adonoy, your God, is giving you and inherit it and live in it, and you say, ‘‘Let me appoint over me a king like all the nations around me;’’
When you enter the land which the Lord your God giveth you, and possess, and dwell in it, and you say, Let us appoint a king over us, like all the nations about me,
17:15: Appoint are you to appoint over yourself a king whom Adonoy, your God, will choose. From among your brothers are you to appoint over yourself a king; you may not [you have no permission to] place over yourself a foreigner who is not your brother.
you shall inquire for instruction before the Lord and afterward appoint the king over you: but it will not be lawful to set over you a foreign man who is not of your brethren.
17:16: However, he must not acquire an abundance of horses for himself so that he will not return the people to Egypt in order to acquire an abundance of horses, because Adonoy told you, ‘‘You are not to proceed to return along this route again.’’

Only let him not increase to him more than two horses, lest his princes ride upon them, and become proud, neglect the words of the law, and commit the sin of the captivity of Mizraim; for the Lord hath told you, By that way ye shall return no more.
17:17: And he is not to acquire an abundance of wives for himself so that his heart will not veer; and silver and gold he may not accumulate for himself in great abundance.

Neither shall he multiply to him wives above eighteen, lest they pervert his heart; nor shall he increase to him silver or gold, lest his heart be greatly lifted up, and he rebel against the God of heaven.
17:18: It shall be, that when he occupies the throne of his kingdom, he must write for himself a duplicate of this Torah in a scroll form [the scroll] before the kohanim—the Levites.

And it shall be that if he be steadfast in the commandments of the law he shall sit upon the throne of his kingdom in security. And let the elders write for him the section (pharasha) of this law in a book before the priests of the tribe of Levi;
17:19: It is to accompany him and he is to read in it all the days of his life, in order that he learn to fear [before] Adonoy, his God, to guard every word of this Torah and these statutes to fulfill them;
and let it be at his side, and he shall read it all the days of his life, that he may learn to fear the Lord his God, to keep all the words of this law, and all these statutes to perform them:
17:20: That his pride not increase over his brothers and he does not stray from the commandment right or left; so that the days of his reign are lengthy over his kingdom, he and his sons within Yisroel.
that his heart may not be arrogant toward his brethren, nor decline from the precepts to the right or the left, and that his days may be prolonged over his kingdom, his and his sons among Israel.
18:1: They will not have—the kohanim, the Levites, the entire tribe of Levi—a portion or an inheritance with Yisroel; Adonoy’s fire-offerings [sacrifices] and His inheritance will they eat.
The priests of the tribe of Levi will have no part or inheritance with their brethren: they shall eat the oblations of the Lord as their portion,

then he shall minister in the Name of the Lord his God as all his brethren the Levites who minister there before the Lord.

When you have entered the land which the Lord your God giveth you, ye shall not learn to do after the abominations of those nations.
18:10: Let there not exist among you anyone who passes his son or daughter through fire, who practices the kosem-occult; who practices time-frame-occult or who divines portentuous events or a sorcerer.

18:11: Or a snake charmer, or one who invokes the spirit of Ov or yidoni, or communicates with the dead.
or make (magical) knots and bindings of serpents and scorpions or any kind of reptile, or who consult the oba, the bones of the dead or the bone Jadua, or who inquire of the manes.

For every one who doeth these is an abomination before the Lord; and because of these abominations the Lord driveth them out before you.
18:13: Walk in perfect trust with [in the fear of] Adonoy, your God.
Ye shall be perfect in the fear of the Lord your God.

a Prophet from among you of your brethren like unto me, with the Holy Spirit will the Lord your God raise up unto you; to Him shall you be obedient.

18:17: Adonoy said to me, ‘‘What they said is excellent.
and the Lord said to me, That which they have spoken is right;

18:19: Now, the man who does not heed My words that he speaks in My Name; I [My word] will demand from him.
and the man who will not hearken to the words of My prophecy which shall be spoken in My Name, My Word shall take vengeance upon him.

19:2: Separate three cities for yourself, within your land that Adonoy, your God, is giving you to inherit.
three cities shall you set apart within your land which the Lord your God giveth you to inherit.
19:3: Ready the route for yourself and divide the borders of your land into three sections that Adonoy, your God, will allot you; this will serve for any murderer to flee there.
You shall prepare a high road, and divide your limit which the Lord your God bestoweth upon you, that any manslayer may flee thither.
19:4: And this is the matter of the murderer who may flee there to survive: whoever smites his peer without intent, and he had not been his enemy yesterday [or] the day before;

And this is the regulation for the manslayer who fleeth thither that he may live: Whoever shall have killed his brother without intention, he not having kept enmity against him yesterday, or the day before,
19:5: And whoever comes with his peer into the woods to chop trees, and as his hand swung the axe downward to cut the wood the iron flew off the wooden handle and encounters his peer and he dies; he is to flee to one of these cities to survive.

(as for example) if any one goeth with his neighbour into the thicket to cut wood, and he driveth his hand with the axe to cut wood, and the iron flieth apart from the haft and lighteth on his neighbour that be die, he may flee to one of those appointed cities, and. save his life.
19:6: Lest the blood-redeemer pursue the murderer when his heart grows heated, and he catches up with him over the length of the road and he smite him dead when he has no [judgment of a] death sentence because he had not been his enemy yesterday [or] the day before.

Lest the avenger of blood follow after him his heart boiling within him on account of his grief, and apprehend him, if the way be long, and take his life, though he is not guilty of the judgment of death, because he had not enmity against him in time past.
19:7: Therefore am I commanding you the following: three cities shall you separate for yourself.
Therefore I command you today that you set apart for you three cities.
19:8: And when Adonoy, your God, expands your boundary, in accordance with His oath to your forefathers, and He give you the entire land that He promised to give to your forefathers,
And if the Lord your God enlarge your border, as He hath sworn to your fathers, and give you all the land which He Hath sworn to your fathers to give,
19:9: When you will be guarding this entire mitzvah to fulfill it, that I am commanding you today, to love Adonoy, your God, and to go in His ways [that are proper before Him] for all time; then you shall add three more cities to these three.

then shall you keep all this commandment which today I command you to do, that thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and walk in the ways which are right before Him all days; and you shall add yet three cities to those three;
19:10: And let innocent blood not be shed within your land that Adonoy, your God, is giving you as territory, [otherwise] you will bear liability for the blood [the judgment of a death sentence].
that innocent blood may not be shed in your land which the Lord your God giveth you to inherit, and the guilt of the judgment of death may not be upon you.
19:11: If there is a man who hates his neighbor, and will ambush him, arising against him and smiting him dead, and he will flee to one of these cities;
But if a man with enmity against his neighbour shall lay wait for him in secret, to destroy his life, and he die, then should he flee into one of those cities,
19:12: The elders of his city will send for and take him from there, and will hand him over to the blood-redeemer, and he will be executed.
the sages of his cities shall send and take him thence, and give him up into the hand of the pursuer for blood, and he shall be put to death.
19:13: Do not view him with compassion. You are to eliminate the [shedding of] innocent blood from Yisroel, and you will have it good.
Your eye shall not spare him, but you shall put away shedders of innocent blood from Israel, that it may be well with you.
19:14: Do not move back the boundary of your neighbor that the first [settlers] determine [bounded] in your territory that you will inherit in the land that Adonoy, your God, is giving you to inherit.
You shall not remove the boundary mark of your neighbours which the predecessors did set for the limit in your possession of inheritance in the land which the Lord your God giveth you to inherit.
19:15: One witness may not arise against a man about any sin or for any transgression or transgression that he transgresses; by the word of two witnesses or by the word of three witnesses let a matter be established.

The testimony of one (witness) shall not be valid against a man for any crime (regarding the taking) of life, or guilt concerning money, or any sin with which one may be charged with sinning; but, by the Word of the Lord, (to insure) retribution upon secret crimes, (while) one witness may swear to deny what hath been attested against him, the sentence shall be confirmed upon the mouth of two witnesses, or of three.
19:16: If false witnesses arise against a man and bear fallacious testimony [with perversity] against him;
When false witnesses stand up against a man to testify wrong things against him,
19:17: The two men shall stand, who are involved in the dispute, before Adonoy, before the kohanim and the judges who are in those days.
then the two men between whom lies the subject of contention shall stand in the presence of the Lord, before the priests and judges who will be in those days:
19:18: When the judges shall investigate thoroughly and behold, the witness testified falsely, they testified falsely against their brother;
and the judges shall question the witnesses of their times fairly; and, behold, false testimony is in the mouth of the witnesses; they have borne false witness against their brother.
19:19: You are to do to [each of] them as he conspired to do to his brother, and eliminate the evil [doers] from among you;
And so shall you do unto them as they had devised to do against their brother, and you shall put down the doers of evil from among you.
19:20: And the remainder will hear and be fearful, and they will not repeat this evil thing among you.
And the wicked who remain will hear and be afraid, and not add to repeat an evil thing like this among you.
19:21: You are not to have compassion: life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.
Your eye shall not spare; life for life, the value of an eye for an eye, the value of a tooth for a tooth, the value of a hand for a hand, the value of a foot for a foot.
20:1: When you go to [wage] war against your enemy, and you see horse and chariot, people who outnumber you; do not be afraid of them, for [the word of] Adonoy, your God, is with you [will aid you], He Who brought you up from the land of Egypt.

When you go forth to battle against your enemies, and see horses and chariots, and peoples proud, overbearing, and stronger than you, fear them not; for all of them are accounted as a single horse and a single chariot before the Lord your God, whose Word will be your Helper; for He brought you free out of the land of Mizraim.
20:2: Now, as you [come] near the battle [to wage war], the kohein shall approach and speak to the people.
And at the time that you draw nigh to do battle, the priest shall approach and speak with the people,
20:3: He will say to them, ‘‘Hear, Yisroel! You are setting out today to battle [to wage war] against your enemies. Do not be faint hearted; or intimidated and do not panic, and do not be crushed [broken] before them;
and say to them, Hear, Israel, you draw near this day to fight against your adversaries; let not your heart be moved, be not afraid, tremble not, nor be broken down before them:
20:4: Because Adonoy, your God, marches with you [before you] to do battle [wage war] for you with your enemies to save you.’’
for the Shekinah of the Lord your God goeth before you to fight for you against your enemies, and to save you.
20:5: The officers will address the people as follows, ‘‘Whichever man has built a new house and did not inaugurate it as a dwelling, let him go and return home lest he die in battle [while waging war] and another man will inaugurate it.

And the officers shall speak with the people, saying: Who is the man who hath builded a new house, and hath not set fast its door-posts to complete it? let him go and return to his house, lest through sin he be slain in the battle, and another man complete it.
20:6: And whichever man has planted a vineyard and did not redeem it[s fruit,] let him go and return home, lest he die in battle [while waging war] and another man redeem it.

Or, what man hath planted a vineyard, and hath not redeemed it from the priest to make it common? let him go and return to his house, lest sin be the occasion of his not redeeming it, but he be slain in the battle, and another make it common.
20:7: And whichever man has betrothed a woman and not married her, let him go and return home, lest he die in battle [while waging war] and another man marry her.’’
And what man hath betrothed a wife, but not taken her? let him go and return to his house, lest sin prevent him from rejoicing with his wife and he be slain in the battle, and another take her.
20:8: The officers will further address the people and say. ‘‘Whoever is afraid or faint [broken] hearted, let him go and return home, and let him not destroy the resolve [break the heart] of his brothers like his own resolve.’’

Yet more shall the officers speak to the people, and say, Who is the man who is afraid on account of his sin and whose heart is broken? let him go and return to his house, that his brethren be not implicated in his sins, and their heart be broken like his.
20:9: When the officers finish addressing the people; they will appoint army commanders at the head of the people.
And when the officers shall have finished to speak with the people, they shall appoint the captains of the host at the head of the people.
20:10: When you near a city to do battle against it, you are to offer it [words of] peace.
When you come nigh to a city to make war against it, then you shall send to it certain to invite it to peace;
20:11: Should it respond, ‘‘Peace!’’ and open for you, then all the people found in it will become your payers of tribute, and your servants.
and if they answer you with words of peace, and open their gates to you, all the people whom you find therein shall be tributaries, and serve you.
20:12: And if it does not settle for peace with you but engages in war against you, you shall lay siege to it.
But if they will not make peace, but war, with you, then you shall beleaguer it.
20:13: Adonoy, your God, will deliver it into your hand, and you will smite all its males by the sword.
And when the Lord your God will have delivered it into your hand, then may you smite every male thereof with the edge of the sword.
20:14: However, the women and the children, and the animals, and everything that will be in the city—all its booty—are you to plunder for yourself; you will eat the booty of your enemies that Adonoy, your God, gave you.
But the women, children, and cattle, and whatever is in the city, even all the spoil, you shall seize, and eat the spoil of your enemies which the Lord your God giveth you.
20:15: So will you do to all the cities, that are very distant from you, that are not among the cities of these nations.
Thus shall you do to all cities that are remote from you, which are not of the cities of these seven nations;
20:16: However, from the cities of these peoples that Adonoy, your God, is giving you as inheritance, you are not to leave any person alive.
but of the cities of these peoples, which the Lord your God giveth you to inherit, ye shall not spare alive any breathing thing:
20:17: Rather annihilate are you to annihilate them: the Chittites and the Emorites, the Canaanites and the Perizites, the Chivites and the Yevusites; as Adonoy, your God, commanded you.
for destroying ye shall destroy them, Hittites, Amorites, Kenaanites, Pherizites, Hivites, and Jebusites, as the Lord your God hath commanded you;
20:18: In order that they do not teach you to do any of their abominations that they did for their gods [idols], and you will sin to [before] Adonoy, your God.
that they may not teach you to do after their abominations with which they have served their idols, and you sin before the Lord your God.
20:19: If you besiege a city many days to wage war against it, to capture it, do not harm [any of] its trees by chopping it with an ax, because you eat from it you are not to cut it down; For, is [not] the tree in the field a man to join the besieged to escape you?

When you beleaguer a city all the seven days to war against it, to subdue it on the Sabbath, you shall not destroy the trees thereof by bringing against them (an instrument of) iron; that you may eat its fruit, cut it not down; for a tree on the face of the field is not as a man to be hidden (put out of sight) before you in the siege.
20:20: Only a tree that you know that it is not a fruit tree may you harm or cut down; and you will build battlements [fortifications] against the city that is waging war against you until it is conquered.
But the tree that you know to be a tree not making fruit to eat, that you may destroy and cut down. And you shall raise bulwarks against the city which maketh war with you, until you have subdued it.
